answer: LinkedIn's Kafka Audit compared counts taken at successive points of its multi-cluster path, not a single cluster's view. Each producer tallied the messages it sent for a topic and reporting interval and periodically published those counts to a dedicated audit topic. Each cluster's Kafka Console Auditor separately consumed topics, accumulated observed counts, and sent audit results; aggregate-cluster auditors counted messages present after MirrorMaker copying; and critical downstream consumers such as Hadoop sinks could publish their own tier counts. Because the counts were for comparable topic and time intervals, the per-tier tallies could be compared along the producer -> local cluster -> aggregate cluster -> critical consumer chain to show where messages were lost or duplicated and at which hop. The page also cautions that equal counts alone cannot prove per-message equality (one lost record can be offset by one duplicate), and clock skew or late producers can make audit windows disagree transiently.
